title: Scene-referred input and working space

ownerDecisions.workingSpace: 2026-11-23: ACEScct is the default working space for color-managed compositions (ACEScg its linear companion); color management stays opt-in per composition; a composition without it renders as before (legacy-srgb).
ownerDecisions.cameraPriority: 2026-11-23: no preference. The nine validated transforms are supported; the seven unavailable ones keep refusing with their reasons.

visualAcceptance: none. Software checks only; no human viewing of any CG7 render.

delivered.colorScience: packages/color-science/src/working-space.ts: working spaces (legacy-srgb, acescct, acescg, linear-bt709), seven conversion spaces (Bradford for a white change), media input transforms with inverses (nine validated camera encodings, D-colour display transfers, BT.2100 PQ with 1.0 = 100 cd/m2, HLG with the reference OOTF at 1000 cd/m2).
delivered.contract: composition colorManagement {workingSpace?} (absent: legacy-srgb; present: ACEScct default); media color adds bt2020/smpte432 primaries, bt2020-10/12, smpte2084, arib-std-b67 transfers, bt2020nc matrix, unspecified tags and an author-declared camera encoding, accepted only with colorManagement; unavailable encodings refused with their reason; warning comp-media-color-declared when a declared encoding contradicts stream tags; grade.color-space-transform 1.0.0 (from/to codes over the seven spaces); LUT inputSpace/outputSpace accept the seven spaces besides legacy-srgb; prepared-media decoder composition-media-decoder-scene-1.
delivered.decode: Video in a color-managed composition: FFmpeg writes 4:4:4 planes at the source depth; Y'CbCr -> RGB and range in float64 from the published equations (camera encodings with full-range equations, the CG0 convention); canonical RGBA16 PNG over [-0.25, 1.25]. Sequences stay RGBA8. Legacy decoder, version and cache keys unchanged.
delivered.render: Every grade run in a color-managed composition converts display -> working on entry and working -> display before its one quantization (neutral runs stay exact copies; lone effects become runs); grade.lut converts to and from its declared spaces; comp grade bake reports the working space its table maps. Video layers draw through a CPU float64 source stage (input transform -> working -> the layer's leading pointwise grade run -> display), identical on Canvas and WebGL2. Page decode of scene frames via DecompressionStream; 8 bytes per live pixel in decodedFrameBytes.
delivered.ce6: Cell catalogue-managed-grade (ACEScct composition: grade.color-space-transform, grade.primary, grade.lut with sRGB-declared spaces) with its own baseline darwin-arm64-managed-grade-1.json.

transforms.evidence: All nine validated camera encodings into ACEScg match the CG0 OpenColorIO end-to-end vectors (AP0 -> AP1) within 2e-5 and round-trip through every working space within 1e-10; every pair of the seven conversion spaces round-trips within 1e-12 and ACEScg -> linear BT.709 equals the CG0 Bradford utility matrix within 1e-12; PQ 58% and HLG 75% decode to 2.03 (203 cd/m2, BT.2408 reference white) within 1%, 38% to 0.26 within 5%; display (encoded sRGB) <-> each managed working space round-trips every tested 8-bit code exactly. The seven unavailable encodings throw in color-science and are refused by validation with their reason. Provenance: packages/color-science/PROVENANCE.md (working-space.ts row).

tenBitLossless.evidence: tests/integration/composition-media-scene.test.ts: all 128 samples of 11 CG0 ramps (8 validated camera curves, PQ, HLG, BT.709; FFV1 10-bit 4:2:2) prepared into the 16-bit scene cache, read back, through the input transform into ACEScct, a neutral grade and back, re-encoded to 10-bit Y' codes by the published equation: every code recovered. Largest cache error 1.144e-5 (bound 1.2e-5). Reference level: the same for all 1024 codes of 12 encodings. Not a file re-encode: 10-bit delivery is CG8, and the existing 10-bit profiles still carry 8-bit pixels.

memory4k.evidence: tests/browser/color-grading-cg7-memory.ts on a generated 3840x2160 10-bit FFV1 clip declared S-Log3 in an ACEScct composition through the real loader (fetch, page decode, source stage): a blended pair is 132,710,400 bytes live (126.6 MiB) within the 128 MiB decodedFrameBytes default on both backends; a 100 MiB budget refuses with comp-media-limit before any frame is fetched (0 fetched); Node preparation checks the RGBA16 budget before FFmpeg runs (integration test). Disk: 2.69 MB per 4K frame for this synthetic source. GPU: the drawn RGBA8 raster is 31.6 MiB, within decodedTextureBytes (128 MiB) by the existing per-texture check; not separately measured. Canvas and WebGL2 output SHA-256 identical. Time: about 2.1 s per 4K frame for the CPU source stage. The source stage's own float64 working set is outside decodedFrameBytes; since the PR #81 review (F2) it runs in row strips of at most 64 Ki pixels (about 2 MiB at any frame size) instead of a whole-frame copy (about 190 MiB at 4K), with identical bytes. Rerun 2026-11-24 (Node 22.23.1): output SHA-256 888d9e1a… on both backends, the same on the pre-merge commit 1c2d7e46, so the earlier recorded f2f81758… was already stale before the merge and the fixes.

parity.summary: Source stage (CPU float64 on both backends): Canvas and WebGL2 equal the float64 reference byte for byte on six ramps, neutral and graded, repeats identical. Display-referred stills graded in ACEScct: Canvas 0, WebGL2 0 from the reference on chart-24, hue-sweep, gray-ramp-256; neutral grade and no grade equal the legacy render. Compositing rule: a translucent solid over a managed video equals the legacy composite of the same display pixels (0). Export via renderComposition png8: 0 on both backends.

compositingRule: Every layer leaves the working space at its boundary through the CG7 display transform (AP1 -> BT.709 Bradford, clip 0-1, sRGB encode); compositing is unchanged. See the decisions, section 4.
deviations: Source stage for video only: sequences are sRGB PNGs by contract and stay display-referred RGBA8 (design note first said every video and sequence).

FFmpeg's RGB64 output was rejected for the scene cache: it widens 10-bit codes by a shift (95 -> 6080 = 95<<6, 1023 -> 65472), so codes above 512 read back one low (53 of 128 S-Log3 ramp samples). The matrix and range now run in float64 in Node.
The source stage runs on the CPU in float64 on both backends (exact, not fast); a GPU source stage is later work.

No tone mapping or gamut compression: the CG7 display transform clips scene values above display white and out-of-gamut colors (CG8 output transforms replace it). Log footage will look clipped in highlights until CG8.
